[LLM] PKINIT Kerberos TGT request via certificate authentication anomaly Actions on Objectives Medium
Detects Kerberos pre-authentication (EID 4768) using PKINIT/certificate where the certificate subject does not match the requesting account — the core behavioural signal of CVE-2022-26923 exploitation and certificate-based account impersonation highlighted in the Unit 42 article. Rationale: Article's Phase 4 explicitly calls out 'Using certificates or keys with public key cryptography for initial authentication (PKINIT) to request Kerberos tickets and impersonate privileged users.' EID 4768 with CertSerialNumber/CertIssuerName/CertThumbprint populated (parsed from EventData XML) is the on-the-wire signature of PKINIT auth — Microsoft documents these fields as part of the 4768 audit event. Cross-referenced with Microsoft MSRC CVE-2022-26923 and MITRE T1649. Cross-checked against: • https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/vulnerability/CVE-2022-26923 • https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/threat-protection/auditing/event-4768 • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1649/
ATT&CKT1558.003 T1649 T1550
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication
IdentityLogonEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where Protocol == "Kerberos"
| where ActionType == "LogonSuccess"
| where AdditionalFields has_any ("PKINIT","Certificate","SmartCard")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| summarize Count = count(), Devices = make_set(DeviceName), IPs = make_set(IPAddress) by AccountName, AccountDomain, bin(Timestamp, 1h)
| where Count > 0
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4768
| extend CertIssuerName = tostring(extract(@"<Data Name=\"CertIssuerName\">([^<]+)<", 1, EventData))
| extend CertSerialNumber = tostring(extract(@"<Data Name=\"CertSerialNumber\">([^<]+)<", 1, EventData))
| extend CertThumbprint = tostring(extract(@"<Data Name=\"CertThumbprint\">([^<]+)<", 1, EventData))
| where isnotempty(CertSerialNumber) or isnotempty(CertThumbprint)
| where TargetUserName !endswith "$"
| summarize TGTCount = count(), Issuers = make_set(CertIssuerName), Serials = make_set(CertSerialNumber), SourceIPs = make_set(IpAddress) by TargetUserName, TargetDomainName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1h)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:windows.security @EventID:4768 (@EventData:*CertSerialNumber* OR @EventData:*CertIssuerName* OR @EventData:*PKINIT*) -@TargetUserName:*$
#event_simpleName=UserLogon
| AuthenticationPackage=/Kerberos/i
| LogonType=2 OR LogonType=3 OR LogonType=10
| (RawEventData=/PKINIT/i OR RawEventData=/CertSerialNumber/i OR RawEventData=/SmartCard/i)
| NOT UserName=/\$$/
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, RemoteAddressIP4], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Authentication.Authentication where Authentication.signature_id=4768 Authentication.authentication_method=*PKINIT* by Authentication.dest Authentication.user Authentication.src Authentication.signature Authentication.authentication_method | `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Authentication.Authentication where Authentication.signature_id=4768 Authentication.authentication_method=*PKINIT* by Authentication.dest Authentication.user Authentication.src Authentication.signature Authentication.authentication_method | `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
[LLM] AD CS certificate request with ENROLLEE_SUPPLIES_SUBJECT flag (ESC1) Exploitation Medium
Detects ESC1-style certificate requests where the requester supplies an arbitrary subject in the Certificate Signing Request — the exact misconfiguration the article describes attackers abusing to mint authentication certificates for high-privilege accounts they don't control. Rationale: Article explicitly calls out the ENROLLEE_SUPPLIES_SUBJECT template flag ('Supply in the request' option) as the key misconfiguration enabling ESC1. EIDs 4886/4887/4888 on AD CS servers carry the Requester and the Attributes blob (parsed from EventData XML) which includes the requested SubjectAltName UPN — a mismatch between Requester and SAN UPN is the textbook ESC1 signal documented by SpecterOps's Certified Pre-Owned research. Cross-checked against: • https://posts.specterops.io/certified-pre-owned-d95910965cd2 • https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/identity/ad-fs/troubleshooting/ad-fs-tshoot-logging • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1649/
ATT&CKT1649 T1078.002
Data sourcesChange.All_Changes
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("CertificateRequest","CertificateIssued")
   or AdditionalFields has_any ("ENROLLEE_SUPPLIES_SUBJECT","CT_FLAG_ENROLLEE_SUPPLIES_SUBJECT")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, AccountDomain, ActionType, AdditionalFields, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID in (4886, 4887, 4888)
| extend Requester = tostring(extract(@"<Data Name=\"Requester\">([^<]+)<", 1, EventData))

| extend TemplateName = tostring(extract(@"<Data Name=\"TemplateName\">([^<]+)<", 1, EventData))

| where Requester !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Requester, RequesterUser, SubjectAltName, SANUser, TemplateName, Attributes, EventData
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")

| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"

        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"

      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")

DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)

| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web

    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`

    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email

         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",

         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

TanStack Npm Packages Compromised Inside The Mini Shai Hulud Supply Chain Attack

Snyk
2026-05-11 12 use cases 5 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

On May 11, 2026, the Mini Shai-Hulud worm compromised 84 npm package artifacts across 42 @tanstack/* packages (as well as @squawk/*, @mistralai/* packages, and others) by chaining a GitHub Actions "Pwn Request," cache poisoning, and OIDC token extraction from runner memory — producing the first npm supply chain attack with valid SLSA Build Level 3 attestations. Here's what happened, what was stolen, and what you need to do right now.

[LLM] Mini Shai-Hulud Wave 4 (TanStack/TeamPCP) worm payload file created in node_modules Installation High
Hunts the smuggled payload artifacts (router_init.js, tanstack_runner.js, vite_setup.mjs) that the May 11 2026 TanStack supply chain attack injected into compromised npm tarballs. These filenames are not declared in any legitimate package.json `files` field, so any FileCreated event for them inside a node_modules path is high-fidelity evidence of an affected install. Rationale: router_init.js / tanstack_runner.js / vite_setup.mjs are explicitly named in the Snyk article as smuggled tarball artifacts and the prepare-hook target (`bun run tanstack_runner.js && exit 1`). They are not in any legitimate TanStack source tree, so a file-creation event under node_modules is a true-positive indicator. Hashes ab4fc...266c and 2ec78d...fc96 are the file SHA256s extracted for this campaign; the master-key hash 0c0e87...da was deliberately excluded (it is a PBKDF2 key, not a file hash). Cross-referenced against prior-session corroboration of the TeamPCP campaign family (mem-obs 305, 317-322) and OSSF MAL-2026-3432 / GHSA-g7cv-rxg3-hmpx. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-g7cv-rxg3-hmpx • https://security.snyk.io/ • https://github.com/ossf/malicious-packages (MAL-2026-3432)
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.007 T1027

[LLM] Session/Oxen P2P exfil DNS or TCP to getsession.org from build/CI host Command & Control High
Hunts the Wave 4 worm's exfiltration channel: encrypted upload to filev2.getsession.org plus seed{1,2,3}.getsession.org Session network nodes. This P2P messenger infrastructure has no legitimate use in CI runners or developer build hosts, and the campaign uses it precisely because IP-blocking is ineffective — DNS is the practical perimeter control. Rationale: filev2.getsession.org and seed{1,2,3}.getsession.org are explicitly named in the Snyk article as the Wave 4 exfil endpoints, with the author noting *.getsession.org DNS-level blocking is the practical perimeter control. Session is a niche P2P messenger; legitimate enterprise CI/build traffic to these domains is effectively zero, giving very high fidelity. Cross-checked against prior-session corroboration of the TeamPCP campaign (mem-obs 305, 317-322) which confirms shared exfil patterns across the Bitwarden CLI / SAP / TanStack waves. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-g7cv-rxg3-hmpx • https://security.snyk.io/ • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog (TeamPCP attribution)
ATT&CKT1090.003 T1041 T1071.004

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) Exploitation High
Browser-pasted PowerShell launched from explorer/Run dialog — ClickFix social engineering.
ATT&CKT1204.004 T1059.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(iex|invoke-expression|frombase64|downloadstring|hxxp|curl |wget )"

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\explorer.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\RuntimeBroker.exe"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(iex|invoke-expression|frombase64|downloadstring|hxxp|curl |wget )"

title: FakeCaptcha / ClickFix - Clipboard-Injected PowerShell from Explorer
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d06
status: experimental
description: |
    "FakeCaptcha" / "ClickFix" social-engineering: malicious site asks
    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1204.002
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\explorer.exe'
            - '\RuntimeBroker.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
    selection_cmd:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'iex'
            - 'invoke-expression'
            - 'frombase64'
            - 'downloadstring'
            - 'hxxp'
            - 'curl '
            - 'wget '
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_cmd
falsepositives:
    - IT-driven scripted automation that admins paste-launch
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",

                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,

| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("799BB5127CA54239D3D4A14367DB3B712012CF14") or SHA1 in~ ("799BB5127CA54239D3D4A14367DB3B712012CF14") or MD5 in~ ("799BB5127CA54239D3D4A14367DB3B712012CF14")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("799BB5127CA54239D3D4A14367DB3B712012CF14") or SHA1 in~ ("799BB5127CA54239D3D4A14367DB3B712012CF14") or MD5 in~ ("799BB5127CA54239D3D4A14367DB3B712012CF14")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["799BB5127CA54239D3D4A14367DB3B712012CF14"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] CL-STA-1132 EarthWorm staging download from 146.70.100.69:8000/php_sess Command & Control High
Hunts outbound HTTP fetches to the CL-STA-1132 EarthWorm staging URL (hxxp://146.70.100.69:8000/php_sess) and to the campaign's other named C2/staging IPs (67.206.213.86, 136.0.8.48, 149.104.66.84). Fires when a compromised PAN-OS firewall — or any internal host laterally pivoted from one — calls back to the attacker's HTTP file-server to retrieve the EarthWorm tunneler. Article-specific because the IP+port+URI triple is unique to this campaign. Rationale: IP triple 146.70.100.69:8000 + URI /php_sess is named explicitly in the Unit 42 brief as the EarthWorm download endpoint — not a generic-noise infrastructure. The other three IPs are listed as direct C2/attacker IPs in the article's IOC table. GitHub Acebond/ReverseSocks5 release URL is also article-named.

[LLM] Malformed CL-STA-1132 attacker User-Agent (Mozilla/5.5 + Safari/532.31) Exploitation High
Hunts the malformed User-Agent the CL-STA-1132 operator used when interacting with the PAN-OS Captive Portal. The string is a forgery — real browsers emit `Mozilla/5.0` (not 5.5) and don't lead with `Safari/532.31`. This UA appearing against any web-facing surface is high-fidelity for either a captive-portal exploit attempt or follow-on operator interaction. Rationale: The UA string `Safari/532.31 Mozilla/5.5 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 ... Chrome/138.0.0.0 Safari/537.36 Edg/138.0.0.0` is reproduced verbatim in the article's IOC table. Both `Mozilla/5.5` (no real browser ships this) and a leading `Safari/532.31` token (real Safari UAs don't lead) make the AND-pair effectively unique to this operator's tooling — a first-time-seen elsewhere is high-fidelity.
ATT&CKT1190 T1071.001
Data sourcesWeb.Web
// Defender XDR has limited HTTP User-Agent visibility outside DeviceNetworkEvents.AdditionalFields
// for HttpConnectionInspected actions; this is best-effort. Pivot to firewall logs in Sentinel for primary coverage.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType == "HttpConnectionInspected"
| extend UA = tostring(parse_json(AdditionalFields).user_agent)
| where UA has "Mozilla/5.5" and UA has "Safari/532.31"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort, UA,
          InitiatingProcessFileName
let MalformedUA1 = "Mozilla/5.5";
let MalformedUA2 = "Safari/532.31";
(union isfuzzy=true
  ( CommonSecurityLog
      | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
      | where RequestClientApplication has MalformedUA1
         and RequestClientApplication has MalformedUA2
      | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, DestinationIP, DestinationPort,
                RequestURL, RequestClientApplication, DeviceVendor,
                DeviceProduct, Activity, _Source="CommonSecurityLog"),
  ( W3CIISLog
      | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
      | where csUserAgent has MalformedUA1
         and csUserAgent has MalformedUA2
      | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP=cIP, DestinationIP=Computer,
                RequestURL=csUriStem, RequestClientApplication=csUserAgent,
                scStatus, _Source="W3CIISLog"))
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] PAN-OS firewall service account LDAP enumeration of DomainDnsZones Actions on Objectives Medium
Hunts the post-exploitation AD recon stage of CL-STA-1132 — using credentials lifted from the compromised firewall to query domain root and DomainDnsZones via LDAP from the firewall's management IP. The article specifies these enumeration targets and the use of the firewall's service-account credentials as the recon vector. Detection joins LDAP/SAMR query telemetry on the service account name from a non-standard / firewall source IP. Rationale: Article explicitly states the operator used `the firewall's service account credentials to target domain root and DomainDnsZones` after compromising PAN-OS. ObjectName-based 4662 with DomainDnsZones is article-named; the SubjectUserName pattern list is the standard PAN-OS LDAP-bind account naming convention (User-ID agents). Sigma omitted because Sigma's logsource model can't cleanly express a 4662-with-ObjectName-substring rule combined with the account-name pattern AND the threshold/aggregation across DCs without backend-specific extensions.
ATT&CKT1087.002 T1018 T1069.002
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication Endpoint.Processes
// Adjust the FirewallSvcAccounts list to your tenant's PAN-OS User-ID / LDAP bind accounts
let FirewallSvcAccounts = dynamic(["panos-svc","panfw","pa-userid","paloalto-bind","fw-svc"]);
let FirewallMgmtIPs   = dynamic([]);  // populate with PAN-OS management IPs
IdentityQueryEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("LDAP query","LDAPQuery","SAMR query")
| where Query has_any ("DomainDnsZones","DC=DomainDnsZones","CN=MicrosoftDNS")
   or QueryTarget has "DomainDnsZones"
| extend AcctLower = tolower(AccountName)
| where AcctLower in (FirewallSvcAccounts)
   or IPAddress in (FirewallMgmtIPs)
   or AccountName has_any ("panos","panfw","paloalto","user-id")
| project Timestamp, AccountName, AccountDomain, AccountUpn,
          DeviceName, IPAddress, ActionType, Query, QueryTarget, Protocol
| order by Timestamp desc
// 4662 = Directory Service Access; AccessMask 0x100 = property read
let FirewallSvcAccountPatterns = dynamic(["panos","panfw","paloalto","pa-userid","user-id","fw-svc"]);
let FirewallMgmtIPs = dynamic([]); // populate with PAN-OS management/data-plane IPs
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4662
| where ObjectName has_any ("DomainDnsZones","DC=DomainDnsZones","MicrosoftDNS")
   or AccessMask has "0x100"
| extend SubjectLower = tolower(SubjectUserName)
| where SubjectLower has_any (FirewallSvcAccountPatterns)
   or IpAddress in (FirewallMgmtIPs)
| summarize ObjectsAccessed = make_set(ObjectName, 25),
            QueryCount = count(),
            FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated),
            LastSeen  = max(TimeGenerated),
            DCs = make_set(Computer)
            by SubjectUserName, SubjectDomainName, IpAddress
| where QueryCount >= 5 or array_length(ObjectsAccessed) >= 3
| order by LastSeen desc
source:windows.security @EventID:4662 AND (@ObjectName:(*DomainDnsZones* OR *MicrosoftDNS*)) AND @SubjectUserName:(*panos* OR *PANOS* OR *panfw* OR *PANFW* OR *paloalto* OR *PaloAlto* OR *user-id* OR *User-ID* OR *fw-svc* OR *FW-SVC*)
ENDPOINT
`wineventlog_security` EventCode=4662 ObjectName="*DomainDnsZones*" OR ObjectName="*CN=Configuration*" OR ObjectName="*DC=*" 
| eval is_fw_account=if(match(SubjectUserName,"(?i)^(panos|panfw|pa-svc|paloalto|fw-svc|user-id).*"),1,0)
| stats min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime count values(ObjectName) as objects values(IpAddress) as src_ip values(Computer) as dc by SubjectUserName SubjectDomainName is_fw_account
| where count > 5 OR is_fw_account=1
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High

ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",

| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,

SecurityEvent

| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"

Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-0300")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-0300")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("e11f69b49b6f2e829454371c31ebf86893f82a042dae3f2faf63dcd84f97a584") or SHA1 in~ ("e11f69b49b6f2e829454371c31ebf86893f82a042dae3f2faf63dcd84f97a584") or MD5 in~ ("e11f69b49b6f2e829454371c31ebf86893f82a042dae3f2faf63dcd84f97a584")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("e11f69b49b6f2e829454371c31ebf86893f82a042dae3f2faf63dcd84f97a584") or SHA1 in~ ("e11f69b49b6f2e829454371c31ebf86893f82a042dae3f2faf63dcd84f97a584") or MD5 in~ ("e11f69b49b6f2e829454371c31ebf86893f82a042dae3f2faf63dcd84f97a584")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["e11f69b49b6f2e829454371c31ebf86893f82a042dae3f2faf63dcd84f97a584"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Copy Fail (CVE-2026-31431) PoC retrieval from copy.fail/exp Delivery High
Detects download of the public Copy Fail proof-of-concept from the copy.fail domain (the URL hard-coded in Xint.Code's published 732-byte Python PoC). Hits curl/wget/python invocations referencing copy.fail in argv. Article-specific because the domain is unique to this CVE; almost any hit is exploitation prep. Rationale: Pivots on the literal string 'copy.fail' which is unique to Xint.Code's published PoC URL referenced in Unit 42's own XQL hunt query (article body, second XQL block: `action_process_image_command_line contains "copy.fail/exp"`). Domain has no legitimate use, so any curl/wget/python referencing it is high-fidelity exploitation prep. No external corroboration available yet — CVE published 2026-04-29 and only Unit 42 has written it up at time of authoring. Cross-checked against: • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/cve-2026-31431-copy-fail/
ATT&CKT1105 T1588.005 T1068

DeviceProcessEvents

         and ProcessCommandLine has "copy.fail")
     or (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("curl","wget","python","python2","python3","python3.8","python3.9","python3.10","python3.11","python3.12")
         and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "copy.fail")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, AccountSid,

ImProcessCreate

| where DvcOs has "Linux" or ActingProcessName startswith "/" or TargetProcessName startswith "/"
| where (TargetProcessName matches regex @"(?i)/(curl|wget|python(\d(\.\d+)?)?)$"
          and TargetProcessCommandLine has "copy.fail")
     or (ActingProcessName matches regex @"(?i)/(curl|wget|python(\d(\.\d+)?)?)$"
          and ActingProcessCommandLine has "copy.fail")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Copy Fail (CVE-2026-31431) - Python interpreter spawning su/sudo/passwd as non-root Exploitation Medium
Detects the documented Copy Fail exploitation pattern: a Python interpreter (the 732-byte PoC script that uses only os/socket/zlib stdlib) spawning su, sudo, or passwd from an unprivileged session. Article-specific because the public PoC is Python-only and the kernel page-cache overwrite must be followed by an immediate exec of the targeted setuid binary to gain UID 0. Complements Unit 42's own Cortex XDR rule by explicitly naming python* parents (their query excludes shells/sudo/su but does not pin python as the high-signal parent). Rationale: Combines two article-specific facts: (1) the public PoC is described as a 732-byte Python script using only stdlib, so the parent of the privilege-escalating su/sudo/passwd call will be a python* binary on virtually all opportunistic exploitation; (2) the kernel-side page-cache modification only matters if the corrupted setuid binary is then exec'd. Unit 42's own published XQL excludes shells/sudo/su as parents but does not pin python — adding the python parent constraint sharpens precision considerably while still being executable on Linux endpoints with EDR, Sysmon-for-Linux, or auditd. Datadog query is parent-less because Datadog's auditd standard schema doesn't ship parent process — it captures the non-root su exec component only and should be paired with an aggregation rule that joins to a parent EXECVE within seconds, or upgraded if the tenant ships Cloud Workload Security events. Cross-checked against: • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/cve-2026-31431-copy-fail/
ATT&CKT1068 T1611 T1548.003

| where InitiatingProcessFileName matches regex @"(?i)^python(\d(\.\d+)?)?$"
| where FileName in~ ("su","sudo","passwd")
| where AccountName !in~ ("root")
| where AccountSid != "0"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, AccountSid,
          ChildBin = FileName, ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine,
          ParentBin = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ParentPath = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          GrandParent = InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName matches regex @"(?i)/python(\d(\.\d+)?)?$"
| where TargetProcessName matches regex @"(?i)/(su|sudo|passwd)$"
| where ActorUsername !in~ ("root")
| where ActorUserId != "0"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActorUserId,
          ParentImage = ActingProcessName, ParentCmd = ActingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage = TargetProcessName, ChildCmd = TargetProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02

            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'

        TargetFilename|endswith:

            - '\Cookies'

level: high

Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:

author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02

logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:

        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'

[LLM] ScarCruft sqgame supply-chain delivery domain contact (BirdCall/RokRAT) Delivery High
Hunts for Windows endpoint or DNS contact with the trojanized Yanbian gaming platform domains (sqgame.net, sqgame.com.cn, xiazai.sqgame.com.cn) which delivered the BirdCall/RokRAT backdoor via a malicious mono.dll update package. Any contact from a managed host warrants investigation as the article confirms the update channel was malicious from late 2024. Rationale: sqgame.net, sqgame.com.cn and xiazai.sqgame.com.cn are explicitly identified by ESET as the supply-chain delivery domains. Any contact is high-fidelity since these are not general-purpose services outside Yanbian-region gamers. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0067/ • https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/rigged-game-scarcruft-compromises-gaming-platform-supply-chain-attack/

[LLM] BirdCall trojanized APK/mono.dll SHA1 match on Windows endpoints Installation High
Alerts on the exact ESET-confirmed SHA1 hashes of the BirdCall-trojanized Yanbian gaming APKs (ybht.apk, sqybhs.apk) appearing on Windows endpoints, or on file events touching the malicious mono.dll update artefact (xiazai.sqgame.com.cn/dating/20240429.zip). Catches enterprise-managed analyst workstations or BYO-laptop sync that pulled the malicious payload. Rationale: Both SHA1 hashes (03E3ECE9F48CF4104AAFC535790CA2FB3C6B26CF and FC0C691DB7E2D2BD3B0B4C1E24D18DF72168B7D9) and the filenames ybht.apk, sqybhs.apk, 20240429.zip are explicitly listed in ESET's IOC table and code blocks. Hash-based file detection has near-zero FP outside of analyst sample handling. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0067/ • https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/rigged-game-scarcruft-compromises-gaming-platform-supply-chain-attack/
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
let BadSha1 = dynamic(["03E3ECE9F48CF4104AAFC535790CA2FB3C6B26CF","FC0C691DB7E2D2BD3B0B4C1E24D18DF72168B7D9"]);
let BadNames = dynamic(["ybht.apk","sqybhs.apk","20240429.zip"]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where SHA1 in~ (BadSha1)
   or FileName in~ (BadNames)
   or (FileName =~ "mono.dll" and FolderPath has "sqgame")
   or FileOriginUrl has_any ("sqgame.net","sqgame.com.cn","xiazai.sqgame.com.cn")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA1, SHA256, FileOriginUrl, FileOriginReferrerUrl, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
let BadSha1 = dynamic(["03E3ECE9F48CF4104AAFC535790CA2FB3C6B26CF","FC0C691DB7E2D2BD3B0B4C1E24D18DF72168B7D9"]);
let BadNames = dynamic(["ybht.apk","sqybhs.apk","20240429.zip"]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadSha1)
   or TargetFileName in~ (BadNames)
   or (TargetFileName =~ "mono.dll" and TargetFilePath has "sqgame")
| project TimeGenerated, Host=DvcHostname, User=ActorUsername, EventType, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA1, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] BirdCall RokRAT cloud-storage C2 beacon (Dropbox/pCloud) from non-browser process Command & Control Medium
Hunts for the BirdCall/RokRAT command-and-control pattern: backdoor processes making API calls to Dropbox or pCloud cloud storage outside of normal browser/sync-client context. ESET explicitly states BirdCall uses Dropbox/pCloud as its primary C2 channel, so non-browser beaconing to api.dropboxapi.com / content.dropboxapi.com / api.pcloud.com from unusual process trees is high-signal. Rationale: ESET explicitly states BirdCall uses Dropbox and pCloud as C2 channels. Pairing the cloud-API destination with a non-browser/non-sync-client process tree is the high-fidelity pivot — bare cloud-API traffic alone is noise. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1102/002/ • https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/rigged-game-scarcruft-compromises-gaming-platform-supply-chain-attack/
ATT&CKT1102.002 T1567.002
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
let CloudC2 = dynamic(["api.dropboxapi.com","content.dropboxapi.com","api.pcloud.com","eapi.pcloud.com","api.pcloud.link"]);
let KnownClients = dynamic(["chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe","iexplore.exe","Dropbox.exe","DropboxUpdate.exe","pCloud.exe","OneDrive.exe","explorer.exe"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any (CloudC2) or tostring(parse_url(RemoteUrl).Host) has_any (CloudC2)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ (KnownClients)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| summarize EventCount=count(), FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp), Urls=make_set(RemoteUrl,10) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| where EventCount >= 3
| order by FirstSeen desc
let CloudC2 = dynamic(["api.dropboxapi.com","content.dropboxapi.com","api.pcloud.com","eapi.pcloud.com","api.pcloud.link"]);
let KnownClients = dynamic(["chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe","iexplore.exe","Dropbox.exe","DropboxUpdate.exe","pCloud.exe","OneDrive.exe","explorer.exe"]);
(union isfuzzy=true
    (ImNetworkSession
     | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
     | where DstHostname has_any (CloudC2) or Url has_any (CloudC2)
     | where ProcessName !in~ (KnownClients)
     | project TimeGenerated, Host=DvcHostname, User=SrcUsername, Process=ProcessName, Cmd=ActingProcessCommandLine, Dst=coalesce(DstHostname,Url), Src="ImNetworkSession"),
    (CommonSecurityLog
     | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
     | where DestinationHostName has_any (CloudC2) or RequestURL has_any (CloudC2)
     | where isnotempty(SourceHostName)
     | extend Process = tostring(split(DeviceCustomString1, "|")[0])
     | where Process !in~ (KnownClients) or isempty(Process)
     | project TimeGenerated, Host=SourceHostName, User=SourceUserName, Process, Cmd=RequestURL, Dst=coalesce(DestinationHostName,RequestURL), Src="CommonSecurityLog"))
| summarize EventCount=count(), FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated), Destinations=make_set(Dst,10) by Host, Process, User
| where EventCount >= 3
| order by FirstSeen desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:3 @DestinationHostname:(*dropboxapi.com OR *api.pcloud.com OR *eapi.pcloud.com OR *api.pcloud.link) -@Image:(*\\chrome.exe OR *\\Chrome.exe OR *\\msedge.exe OR *\\firefox.exe OR *\\Firefox.exe OR *\\Dropbox.exe OR *\\pCloud.exe OR *\\OneDrive.exe OR *\\explorer.exe)
#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/(dropboxapi\.com|api\.pcloud\.com|eapi\.pcloud\.com|api\.pcloud\.link)$/i
| ContextImageFileName!=/\\(chrome|msedge|firefox|brave|opera|iexplore|Dropbox|DropboxUpdate|pCloud|OneDrive|explorer)\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, DomainName], function=count())
| _count > 2

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

title: Obfuscated / Encoded PowerShell Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d08
status: experimental

    window, no-profile, bypass policy, IEX / Invoke-Expression / Net
    .WebClient.DownloadString — combinations indicating evasion.

    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
